questions.description: 1938-巴西-民俗研究-任务-记录音乐

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先介绍1938年的巴西民俗研究任务，然后解释其目的是尽快记录音乐，接着描述他们记录了什么内容，最后说明这些收集的资料最终被束之高阁。段落2是开头，因为它引入了时间和主题；段落1是对任务目的的解释；段落3描述了具体行动；段落4是结果。
answer.explanation: 段落2是开头，因为它引入了时间和主题；段落1是对任务目的的解释；段落3描述了具体行动；段落4是结果。

questions.title: Green Technology Engineering

paragraphs.text: Engineers are much needed to develop greener technologies.
The energy sector has a fantastic skills shortage at all levels, both now and looming over it for the next 10 years
Not only are there some good career opportunities, but there's a lot of money going into the research side, too.
With the pressures of climate change and the energy gap, in the last few years funding from the research councils has probably doubled.

questions.description: 工程师---未来10年---工作机会-----收入翻倍

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明工程师在开发绿色技术中的需求，然后指出能源行业未来10年的技能短缺，接着提到工作机会和研究资金的增加，最后说明由于气候变化和能源缺口，研究资金在过去几年可能翻倍。段落1是开头，因为它引入了主题；段落2描述了行业背景；段落3说明了机会；段落4是结果和原因。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它引入了工程师开发绿色技术的主题；段落2描述了能源行业未来10年的技能短缺背景；段落3说明了工作机会和研究资金的增加；段落4是结果，解释了由于气候变化和能源缺口导致资金翻倍的原因。

questions.title: Employee Motivation Management

paragraphs.text: In order to do this, the manager should be able to motivate its employees.
The job of a manager in the workplace is to get things done through the employees.
However, this easier said than done.
Motivation practice and theory are difficult, complex subjects touching on several disciplines.

questions.description: 经理----激励员工----简单----难

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明经理在工作场所通过员工完成任务的职责，然后指出经理需要激励员工，接着提到这说起来容易做起来难，最后说明激励的实践和理论是复杂的多学科课题。段落2是开头，因为它定义了经理的职责；段落1是对职责的具体要求；段落3指出执行的难度；段落4是深层原因和总结。
answer.explanation: 段落2是开头，因为它定义了经理通过员工完成任务的职责；段落1具体说明了激励员工的要求；段落3指出说起来容易做起来难的现实；段落4是结果，解释激励涉及复杂理论和多学科的原因。

questions.title: Energy Research Career

paragraphs.text: Many countries are suffering a shortage of scholars of new energy.
Becoming an engineer not only means more opportunities in their career but will gain more money in their research.
The money distributed in energy research will double.
Especially engineers about new energy with the climate change.

questions.description: 许多国家-工程师-想要钱-想要更多钱

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先指出许多国家缺乏新能源学者，然后提到特别是新能源工程师在气候变化背景下的需求，接着说明能源研究资金将翻倍，最后说明成为工程师不仅带来更多职业机会还能获得更多研究资金。段落1是开头，因为它引入了主题；段落4具体化需求；段落3说明资金增长；段落2是结果和优势。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它引入了许多国家缺乏新能源学者的主题；段落4具体说明新能源工程师在气候变化中的需求；段落3指出能源研究资金将翻倍；段落2是结果，说明工程师的职业机会和资金优势。

questions.title: Scottish Banking History

paragraphs.text: When this bank was founded in 1695, Scots coinage was in short supply and of uncertain value, compared with English, Dutch, Flemish or French c 1 oin.
In most countries it is only the government, through their central banks, who are permitted to issue currency.
But in Scotland three banks are still allowed to issue banknotes.
To face growth of trade it was deemed necessary to remedy this lack of an adequate currency.
The first Scottish bank to do this was the Bank of Scotland.

questions.description: 许多国家-三个银行-两个银行-一个银行-null银行

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明大多数国家只有中央银行发行货币，然后提到苏格兰仍有三家银行可以发行钞票，接着指出第一家这样做的苏格兰银行是苏格兰银行，再说明该银行成立于1695年，当时货币短缺，最后提到贸易增长需要解决货币不足问题。段落2是开头，因为它介绍了普遍规则；段落3提到苏格兰的例外；段落5具体到第一家银行；段落1提供历史背景；段落4是目的和结果。
answer.explanation: 段落2是开头，因为它介绍了大多数国家由中央银行发行货币的普遍规则；段落3提到苏格兰三家银行的例外情况；段落5具体指出苏格兰银行是第一家；段落1提供1695年的历史背景；段落4是结果，说明贸易增长需要解决货币问题。

questions.title: Foreign Aid Evolution

paragraphs.text: Although the system is far from perfect, it is certainly more transparent than it was when foreign aid routinely helped ruthless dictators stay in power.
Scrutiny by the news media shamed many developed countries into curbing their bad practices.
Today, the projects of organizations like the World Bank are meticulously inspected by watchdog groups.
By the beginning in the 1990s, foreign aid began to slowly improve.

questions.description: 1990-bad-today-perfect

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是从1990年代初外国援助开始缓慢改善开始，然后提到新闻媒体的监督促使发达国家减少不良做法，接着说明如今世界银行等组织的项目受到严格检查，最后指出现在的系统虽不完美但比过去透明得多。段落4是开头，因为它提供了时间起点；段落2说明改进的推动力；段落3描述当前情况；段落1是总结和对比。
answer.explanation: 段落4是开头，因为它提供了1990年代初的时间起点；段落2说明新闻媒体监督推动了改进；段落3描述如今的严格检查现状；段落1是结果，总结系统虽不完美但比过去更透明。

questions.title: Television's Impact on Society

paragraphs.text: Television hasn't been with us all that long, but we are already beginning to forget what the world was like without it. Before we admitted the one-eyed monster into our homes, we never found it difficult to occupy our spare time. We used to enjoy civilized pleasures. For instance, we used to have hobbies, we used to entertain our friends and be entertained by them, we used to go outside for our amusements to theatres, cinemas, restaurants and sporting events.

We even used to read books and listen to music and broadcast talks occasionally. All that belongs to the past. Now all our free time is regulated by the goggle box. We rush home or gulp down our meals to be in time for this or that programme.
Whole generations are growing up addicted to the telly. Food is left uneaten, homework undone and sleep is lost.

We have even given up sitting at table and having a leisurely evening meal, exchanging the news of the day. A sandwich and a glass of beer will do—anything, providing it don't interfere with the programme. The monster demands and obtains absolute silence and attention.
If any member of the family dares to open his mouth during a programme, he is quickly silenced.

questions.description: 电视---广播- 放弃了---一些家庭---甚至是后代

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先回忆电视出现前人们的生活方式，然后提到电视取代了过去的娱乐活动如读书和听音乐，接着说明人们放弃了悠闲的晚餐时间以观看节目，再指出家庭成员在节目期间必须保持安静，最后提到整代人都沉迷于电视。段落1是开头，因为它引入了电视前的生活；段落2描述电视取代旧习惯；段落4具体到晚餐变化；段落5提到家庭规则；段落3是广泛影响的结果。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它引入了电视出现前的生活方式；段落2描述电视如何取代读书等活动；段落4具体说明放弃悠闲晚餐的影响；段落5提到家庭成员在节目期间的规则；段落3是结果，指出整代人的沉迷。

questions.title: Snake Removal Incident

paragraphs.text: Big Country Snake Removal responded to a home in Albany, Texas, after a man who was trying to restore his cable, climbed under the house and saw some snakes.
"He saw a 'few' snakes and quickly crawled out," said a post on Big Country Snake Removal's Facebook page.
"We arrived around lunchtime and as soon as I crawled under I could immediately see that there was far more than a 'few,'" the post said.
The company ended up removing 45 rattlesnakes from beneath the house.

questions.description: 得克萨斯 男---脸书----午饭的时候-45条舍

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先描述得克萨斯州一名男子因修电缆发现蛇并呼叫Big Country Snake Removal，然后引用脸书帖子说明男子看到‘几条’蛇后爬出，接着救援人员在午饭时到达并发现远不止‘几条’，最后说明公司移除了45条响尾蛇。段落2是开头，因为它介绍了事件起因；段落1是脸书引述的细节；段落3描述救援行动；段落4是结果。
answer.explanation: 段落2是开头，因为它介绍了得克萨斯男子发现蛇的事件起因；段落1引用脸书帖子提供细节；段落3描述救援人员到达和发现；段落4是结果，说明移除了45条响尾蛇。

questions.title: Importance of Vaccination

paragraphs.text: Vaccines are very important to this effort.
They protect children from getting and spreading diseases that can make them very sick.
For this reason, we require children aged 2–months to 18–years old who are entering or attending child care, public school, or private school be vaccinated against certain diseases.
A healthy school setting gives all students the best chance to learn and grow.

questions.description: 学校里---打疫苗---保护学生---这个原因

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明健康的学校环境为学生提供最佳学习机会，然后指出疫苗对此努力很重要，接着描述疫苗如何保护儿童免受疾病侵害，最后说明因此要求2个月至18岁的儿童接种疫苗。段落4是开头，因为它引入了学校环境的主题；段落1说明疫苗的重要性；段落2具体描述保护作用；段落3是结果和政策。
answer.explanation: 段落4是开头，因为它引入了健康学校环境的主题；段落1指出疫苗对这一目标的重要性；段落2具体说明疫苗的保护作用；段落3是结果，解释因此制定了疫苗要求政策。

questions.title: Innovative Textile Development

paragraphs.text: Fibers suitable for clothing have been made for the first time from the wheat protein gluten.
The fibers are as strong and soft as wool and silk.
But they are up to 30 times cheaper.

Narenda Reddy and Yiqi Yang, who produced the fibers at the University of Nebraska in Lincoln, say that because they are biodegradable they might be used in biomedical applications such as surgical sutures.

questions.description: 蛋白质-让人变强-30倍-不信问杨

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先介绍首次从小麦蛋白质中制造出适合服装的纤维，然后说明这些纤维像羊毛和丝绸一样坚韧柔软，接着指出它们便宜30倍，最后提到内布拉斯加大学的两位研究者认为其可生物降解性可用于医疗用途。段落2是开头，因为它引入了创新；段落1描述纤维特性；段落3说明成本优势；段落4是研究者和应用前景。
answer.explanation: 段落2是开头，因为它介绍了从小麦蛋白质制造纤维的创新；段落1描述纤维像羊毛和丝绸的特性；段落3指出成本便宜30倍；段落4是结果，提到研究者和潜在医疗应用。

questions.title: Workplace Performance Issues

paragraphs.text: They go to work very early, from 7:00 to 8:00.
And they went home very late, some even overwork.
Because of great demand, more and more employees are putting themselves into limit.
Many managers find the employee's performance column is decreasing.
They (managers) should avoid this phenomenon, because this is not good for the company.

questions.description: 打工人-起早-贪黑-老板-觉得不行

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明由于巨大需求员工将自己推向极限，然后提到他们早起工作，接着描述他们晚归甚至加班，最后指出经理发现员工表现下降并认为应避免此现象。段落3是开头，因为它介绍了需求背景；段落1描述早起；段落2说明晚归；段落4是经理的观察；段落5是建议和结果。
answer.explanation: 段落3是开头，因为它介绍了巨大需求导致员工极限工作的背景；段落1描述员工早起；段落2说明晚归和加班；段落4是经理发现表现下降；段落5是结果，建议避免此现象。

questions.title: Job Satisfaction Factors

paragraphs.text: Numbers of staff who wish to turn up and do a simple job and go home is relatively happy if they believe their work is secure.
However, any employee who wants to acquire more varied and responsible duties will not feel satisfied for long staying with the same and boring job.
People want to keep working hard only if there are opportunities for promotion to a more challenging job.
If this opportunity does not exist, they are most likely to be demotivated.

questions.description: 简单工作-无聊-难得工作挑战-不存在

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明希望做简单工作并相信工作稳定的员工相对满意，然后指出想要更多职责的员工对单调工作不满意，接着提到只有晋升机会才能激励努力工作，最后说明如果没有机会员工会失去动力。段落1是开头，因为它介绍了满意的员工类型；段落2对比不满意的类型；段落4说明激励条件；段落3是结果。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它介绍了对简单工作满意的员工；段落2对比那些对单调工作不满意的员工；段落4说明晋升机会是激励条件；段落3是结果，指出无机会导致动力丧失。

questions.title: Desert Music Festival

paragraphs.text: The 'Festival in The Desert' is a celebration of the musical heritage of the Touareg, a fiercely independent nomadic people.
It is held annually near Essakane, an oasis some 40 miles north–west of Timbuktu, the ancient city on the Niger River.
Reaching it tests endurance, with miles of impermanent sand tracks to negotiate.
The reward of navigating this rough terrain comes in the form of a three-day feast of music and dance.

questions.description: 沙漠--一年一次40mile-只要到了-就有奖励

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先介绍‘沙漠节’庆祝图阿雷格人的音乐遗产，然后说明它每年在廷巴克图西北40英里的绿洲举行，接着描述到达那里的沙路考验耐力，最后指出克服地形困难的奖励是三天的音乐舞蹈盛宴。段落1是开头，因为它引入了节日主题；段落3提供地点和时间；段落2描述旅途挑战；段落4是结果和奖励。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它介绍了沙漠节的主题；段落3提供每年在绿洲举行的具体信息；段落2描述到达的沙路挑战；段落4是结果，说明奖励是音乐舞蹈盛宴。

questions.title: Archaeological Dating Methods

paragraphs.text: The series of strata in an archaeological dig enables an excavator to date recovered objects relatively, if not absolutely.
However, when archaeologists want to know the absolute date of a site, they can often go beyond simple stratigraphy.
Historical records, coins, and other date–bearing objects can help — if they exist. But even prehistoric sites contain records written in nature's hand.

For example, tree ring, Dendrochronology (literally, tree time) dates wooden artefacts by matching their ring patterns to known records, which, in some areas of the world, span several thousand years.

questions.description: 硬币coin-能够enable-跨越go beyond-千年 thousands

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明历史记录和硬币等物件可帮助确定日期，然后指出地层序列能相对或绝对地确定挖掘物年代，接着提到考古学家可超越简单地层学来确定绝对日期，最后举例树轮年代学如何通过环纹匹配确定木制文物年代。段落3是开头，因为它介绍了基本方法；段落1说明地层序列的作用；段落2提到超越地层学；段落4是具体实例和结果。
answer.explanation: 段落3是开头，因为它介绍了硬币等历史记录的基本方法；段落1说明地层序列的相对和绝对作用；段落2提到超越简单地层学的能力；段落4是结果，举例树轮年代学确定千年文物。

questions.title: Electronic Waste Growth

paragraphs.text: The global market for electrical and electronic equipment continues to expand, while the lifespan of many products becomes shorter.
The current global production of e-waste is estimated to be 20–25 million tonnes per year, with most e-waste being produced in Europe, the United States and Australasia.
In Europe e-waste is increasing at three to five percent a year, almost three times faster than the total waste stream.
Developing countries are also expected to triple their e-waste production over the next five years.

questions.description: 全球-欧美澳-欧美澳-发展中国家

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明电子设备市场扩张和产品寿命缩短，然后估计当前全球每年产生2000-2500万吨电子垃圾，接着指出欧洲电子垃圾增长速度是总垃圾的三倍，最后提到发展中国家未来五年电子垃圾预计增加三倍。段落1是开头，因为它引入了主题；段落2提供全球数据；段落3具体到欧洲；段落4是发展中国家的预测结果。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它介绍了电子设备市场和寿命的主题；段落2提供全球电子垃圾的估计数据；段落3具体说明欧洲的增长速度；段落4是结果，预测发展中国家的三倍增长。

questions.title: Mink Ecology in Iceland

paragraphs.text: The American mink has been present in Iceland since the 1930's and despite heavy hunting since 1939 the species has become well established.
Iceland is therefore an ideal place to study undisturbed feeding behaviour and ecology of mink.
The ecosystem in Iceland is simpler than in other areas where mink are found; the only other mammalian predator is the arctic fox.
Direct competition between these species appears to be minimal although the arctic fox will sometimes chase mink and disturb them while foraging.

questions.description: 美国的--生态系统-似乎appears to be -理想的ideal 或者记mink mink出现的早的放前面

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明美国水貂自1930年代在冰岛存在并已建立种群，然后指出冰岛生态系统简单只有北极狐作为其他哺乳动物掠食者，接着提到两者竞争似乎很小但北极狐会干扰水貂觅食，最后说明冰岛因此是研究水貂行为和生态的理想地点。段落1是开头，因为它介绍了水貂的历史；段落3描述生态背景；段落4说明竞争关系；段落2是结果和意义。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它介绍了美国水貂在冰岛的历史；段落3描述冰岛简单的生态系统；段落4说明水貂和北极狐的竞争关系；段落2是结果，指出冰岛是研究水貂的理想地点。

questions.title: Sea Turtle Shell Sensitivity

paragraphs.text: The bony shell of a sea turtle can actually sense when something touches it.
A series of thin nerves run along the shell and detect pressure changes associated with touch.

The nerves do not contain pain receptors so scientists do not think sea turtles feel pain when touched on the shell, but these thin nerves could transmit information to other parts of the sea turtle's body.
In addition, researchers and scuba divers have observed sea turtles respond to the stimulation of being touched on the skin of their head and their flippers.

questions.description: 海龟-跑了-痛苦的-研究院

questions.title: Gender-Typed Toys Impact

paragraphs.text: Gender–typed toy play leads to the promotion of different skills in boys and girls, with girls practicing communal roles and boys practicing agentic roles.

Whereas play with stereotypically masculine toys, such as blocks and toy soldiers, is generally associated with the development of spatial skills and more aggressive behavior, playing with stereotypically feminine toys, such as baby dolls and stuffed animals, is associated with more nurturing behavior.
In general, strongly gender–typed toys are less supportive of the development of children's physical, cognitive, and artistic skills than are gender–neutral or moderately gender–typed toys.

Therefore, playing predominantly with same–gender–typed toys limits the development of children's action repertoires in accordance with gender stereotypes and thus contributes to the perpetuation of gender stereotypes.
This guides children's activities in accordance with gender stereotypes and thus restricts their individual development potential.
Play with sexualized dolls, such as Fashion Barbies, is even associated with a narrowing of perceived career options in girls.

paragraphs.text: Researchers found that employee productivity is related to their ability to see greenery in office and the natural environment outside.
Poor lighting and no greenery will cause low efficiency and lack of concentration.
A study in the United States found that adding green plants to office spaces could reduce employees’ sick leave and improve workplace efficiency.
Another study found that artificial green plants, such as high-resolution images and TV displays, can have the same effect even if there are no windows.
Some places do not have windows, and are unable to have green plants.

questions.description: 绿植-效率-窗户-人工绿植

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明绿色环境与员工生产力有关，然后指出光线不足和没有绿植会导致效率低、注意力不集中，接着补充有绿植时效率更高。之后说明有些地方没有窗户、无法摆放真实绿植，最后引出人工绿植、高清图片或电视画面也能产生相同效果。
answer.explanation: 段落1介绍绿色环境与员工生产力的关系；段落2说明没有良好光线和绿植的负面影响；段落3补充绿植能提高效率；段落5提出没有窗户的限制；段落4用另一项研究说明人工绿植和屏幕画面可以解决这一问题。

questions.title: Tectonic Plate Movement and Its Effects

paragraphs.text: The movement also creates gaps in tectonic plates, which reduce the pressure on the mantle beneath it, allowing it to melt and push through.
The buildup and sudden release of friction from this movement can cause earthquakes.
This leads the tectonic plates on top to slowly jostle one another.
The mantle makes up 84 percent of Earth’s volume, and though it’s solid rock, over the course of millions of years, it behaves like a liquid.

questions.description: 地壳运动 - 板块 - 地震 - 地幔

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先介绍地幔的特性，然后说明板块的移动导致相互挤压，接着提到摩擦释放引发地震，最后指出板块间隙使地幔熔化并上涌。段落4是开头，因为它介绍了地幔的特性；段落3说明板块移动的结果；段落2描述地震的成因；段落1是最终结果，解释地幔熔化和上涌的过程。
answer.explanation: 段落4是开头，因为它介绍了地幔的特性，为板块运动提供背景；段落3说明板块移动导致相互挤压；段落2描述摩擦释放引发的地震；段落1是结果，解释板块间隙使地幔熔化并上涌的过程。

questions.title: Teaching and Learning Relationship

paragraphs.text: However, most of what we learn before, during, and after attending schools is learned without its being taught to us.
Traditional education focuses on teaching, not learning.
A child learns such fundamental things as how to walk, talk, eat, dress, and so on without being taught these things.
It incorrectly assumes that for every ounce of teaching there is an ounce of learning by those who are taught.

questions.description: Traditional education → incorrectly assumes → however → a child learns

answer.translation: 传统教育关注的是教学，而不是学习。它错误地认为，对于每一分教学，被教的人就会获得相应的一分学习。然而，我们在上学前、上学期间以及离开学校后所学到的大部分内容，并不是别人教给我们的。儿童无需被专门教授，就能学会走路、说话、吃饭、穿衣等基本能力。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它提出核心观点：传统教育更重视教学而不是学习。段落2紧接着说明这种传统观念中的错误假设，即认为教学的多少会直接等同于学习的多少。段落3用 However 形成转折，指出实际上很多学习并不依赖正式教学。段落4进一步举例说明，儿童在没有被专门教授的情况下，也能自然学会走路、说话、吃饭、穿衣等基本能力，因此作为对段落3观点的具体支持。

questions.title: Toys and Gender Stereotypes

paragraphs.text: However, toys do more than just for fun.
Parents often buy toys based on gender stereotypes.
Toys are not only for entertainment, but also bring skill developments.
For example, they buy cars for boys and dolls for girls.

questions.description: Parents often buy toys → For example → However → Toys are not only

answer.translation: 父母通常会根据性别刻板印象给孩子购买玩具。例如，他们会给男孩买玩具车，给女孩买洋娃娃。然而，玩具的作用不仅仅是为了好玩。玩具不仅是为了娱乐，还能带来技能的发展。

questions.title: Proteins and Plant Growth

paragraphs.text: Understanding this process helps researchers find that some grains can live in drought.
Researchers find proteins can regulate plant growth.
In the future this can be applied to crops across the world so they can adapt to drought.
They can help plant roots adapt to climate.

questions.description: Researchers find proteins → They can help roots → Understanding this process → In the future

answer.translation: 研究人员发现蛋白质可以调节植物生长。它们可以帮助植物根部适应气候。理解这一过程有助于研究人员发现，一些谷物可以在干旱环境中生存。未来，这一发现可以应用于世界各地的农作物，使它们能够适应干旱。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，因为它提出核心发现：蛋白质可以调节植物生长。段落2中的 They 指代前一句中的 proteins，因此应紧跟段落1，说明这些蛋白质可以帮助植物根部适应气候。段落3进一步说明理解这一过程带来的研究意义，即帮助发现某些谷物可以在干旱中生存。段落4用 In the future 引出未来应用，因此放在最后，说明这一发现未来可以用于全球农作物，使其适应干旱。

questions.title: First-Language Learning and Raising Children

paragraphs.text: Another way in which most people encounter first-language learning is in raising children.
Of course you don't have to know linguistics to know how to "teach" a baby a language; babies aren't really taught language anyway.
But knowing what it is that babies learn when they learn a language can make the process more enjoyable.

You'll be able to better appreciate what an amazing process learning a language is, why so many people are fascinated with how this process happens, how your baby does the same kinds of things that others do and, at the same time, how your baby's learning steps are unique.

questions.description: 第一语言学习 - 养育孩子 - 不需要语言学知识 - 理解学习过程 - 欣赏婴儿语言发展

answer.translation: 这个段落的正确顺序是先说明人们接触第一语言学习的另一种方式是养育孩子；然后说明你不需要懂语言学也可以知道如何“教”婴儿语言，因为婴儿其实并不是被真正教会语言的；接着指出，如果了解婴儿学习语言时到底学到了什么，这个过程会变得更有趣；最后说明这样你就能更好地欣赏语言学习这一惊人的过程，理解为什么很多人对这一过程着迷，也能看到你的宝宝既和其他宝宝有相似的发展方式，又有自己独特的学习步骤。
answer.explanation: 段落1是开头，引出主题：通过养育孩子接触第一语言学习。段落2进一步说明普通人不需要语言学知识也能参与婴儿语言发展。段落3形成转折，指出了解婴儿到底学了什么会让这个过程更有趣。段落4是结果和展开，说明这种理解能帮助父母更好地欣赏语言学习过程，并看到宝宝语言发展的普遍性和独特性。

questions.title: Cutting fund from Ontario community preschool
questions.summary: Cutting fund from Ontario community preschool will negatively affect early childhood educator and their families.
questions.text:
Cutting fund from Ontario community preschool will negatively affect early childhood educator and their families. When funding is reduced, community preschools struggle to maintain operations, and this creates immediate pressure on both childcare access and service quality for local families. Some centres may raise fees or close programs, making it harder for parents to find affordable and stable early learning options.

In addition to limiting access, funding cuts directly weaken the financial stability and career development of early childhood educators. Without consistent provincial support, staff lose wage enhancements and training opportunities, leading to heavier workloads, lower job satisfaction, and increasing turnover across the sector.

 Stable and adequate funding is essential to protect educators’ livelihoods and to support the long-term well-being of families and communities. Advocacy groups in Ontario emphasize that investing in preschool programs is not just an expense, but a foundation for social development, workforce participation, and high-quality early education for children.

questions.title: Microloans
questions.summary:
Business microloans have emerged as a powerful tool for supporting small enterprises and fostering economic growth, particularly in developing countries. These small, short-term loans are designed to provide entrepreneurs with the necessary capital to start or expand their businesses. Microloans often have lower interest rates compared to traditional loans, making them more accessible to individuals who might not qualify for conventional financing. The impact of microloans can be profound, as they enable entrepreneurs to purchase equipment, hire employees, and increase production, ultimately contributing to the overall economy. 
 
One of the key benefits of business microloans is their ability to empower marginalized groups, including women and minorities, by providing them with the financial resources to achieve economic independence. Many microloan programs specifically target these groups, recognizing that they often face greater barriers to accessing traditional financial services. By supporting these entrepreneurs, microloans can help reduce poverty and promote social inclusion.
 
However, there are also challenges associated with microloans. Some critics argue that the small loan amounts and short repayment periods can place undue pressure on borrowers, potentially leading to financial strain and default. Additionally, the success of microloan programs often depends on the availability of complementary services, such as financial literacy training and business development support, to ensure that borrowers can effectively manage their loans and grow their businesses.
 
 Despite these challenges, business microloans remain a vital tool for promoting entrepreneurship and economic development. As more financial institutions and non-profit organizations recognize the value of microloans, it is essential to continue refining and expanding these programs to maximize their impact on communities around the world.

questions.text:
If someone used your card to purchase a car without your permission, who might be your family members, you should contact your bank.

Online shopping has become increasingly popular due to its convenience, allowing consumers to purchase a wide range of products from the comfort of their homes. However, cases of unauthorized transactions, such as when someone uses your credit card to buy a car without your permission, can occur. It is important to report such incidents promptly to your bank to initiate an investigation and potentially recover the lost funds.

In cases where the unauthorized transaction is conducted by a family member, immediate contact with the bank is not advised. Involving the bank could lead to police intervention, as unauthorized use of a credit card is legally considered theft, even among family members. Therefore, it is recommended to resolve the matter privately if possible before escalating it officially. Another situation arises when a friend or acquaintance uses your card with or without your explicit consent. Depending on the circumstances, you may need to evaluate whether to pursue legal action or seek an informal resolution. Each scenario requires careful consideration of the relationship and the potential legal implications.

questions.title: Children need to explore outdoors
questions.summary: Children need to explore outdoors to develop their physical and mental abilities.
questions.text:
Previously, children had plenty of time to play outside, but now many parents often urge them by saying, “Hurry up, don’t be late for class.” As a result, children spend less time in nature and more time rushing between structured activities, losing opportunities to explore freely and enjoy the outdoors.

This reduced contact with nature has consequences for children’s development, as a lack of outdoor play limits creativity, physical activity, and emotional regulation. When schedules are filled with classes and academic pressure, children miss important moments to observe the world, build independence, and learn through sensory experiences.

Balancing academic learning with outdoor experiences is essential to support healthy childhood growth. By allowing children more time in nature, families and communities can help them develop curiosity, resilience, and a stronger connection to the environment.

questions.title: Business opening
questions.summary: A good business opening can increase sales and revenue. On the first day of business opening, you can give some discounts and do some special activities to attract customers
questions.text:
Opening a new business is an exciting yet challenging endeavor that requires meticulous planning and strategic execution. One of the crucial aspects of launching a new business is making a memorable impression on your big day, also known as the grand opening. This event not only serves as the official introduction of your business to the public but also sets the tone for your brand's identity and customer experience. To ensure a successful grand opening, it is essential to offer enticing incentives and activities that will attract potential customers and create a buzz around your business. 

Consider offering exclusive discounts or special promotions to attendees, which can encourage them to make purchases and spread the word about your business. Additionally, providing free samples or demonstrations of your products or services can give guests a firsthand experience of what your business has to offer. Hosting engaging activities, such as live music, games, or interactive workshops, can also enhance the overall atmosphere and make the event more enjoyable for guests.

Another effective strategy is to offer giveaways or raffles with attractive prizes, which can incentivize attendees to participate and stay longer at your event. Collaborating with local influencers or community leaders can further amplify your reach and attract a larger crowd. Ensuring that your event is well-organized and staffed will contribute to a positive experience for your guests, leaving a lasting impression that encourages them to return. Ultimately, a successful grand opening is about creating a welcoming and memorable experience for your guests, showcasing the unique value of your business, and building a foundation for long-term customer relationships. By offering appealing incentives and engaging activities, you can generate excitement and establish a strong presence in your community.

questions.title: Climate Change
questions.summary: Climate change represents one of the most significant challenges facing humanity today. Rising global temperatures, caused primarily by greenhouse gas emissions, are leading to more frequent extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and disruptions to ecosystems worldwide. The impacts extend beyond environmental concerns to affect human health, food security, and economic stability. Addressing climate change requires coordinated international efforts to reduce carbon emissions, develop renewable energy sources, and implement sustainable practices across all sectors of society. While the challenge is immense, technological innovations and growing public awareness offer hope for meaningful progress.

questions.title: esports
questions.text:
In recent years, Esports has become increasingly recognized by schools as an educational opportunity rather than just entertainment. Many high schools and colleges now offer Esports programs, training spaces, and official teams, showing that educators understand the growing influence of gaming in society. These programs also allow students who are not interested in traditional sports to participate in group activities and feel included at school.
 
Participating in Esports can help students build confidence, teamwork skills, and a sense of belonging. Team members learn how to communicate under pressure, practice regularly to improve their performance, and support each other just like athletes in physical sports. These experiences are especially valuable for students who might feel shy or disconnected, and success in competitions often motivates them to be more active and focused in their academic life.

Research and school reports show that Esports programs can even improve academic outcomes and increase graduation rates. Students involved in Esports are often more willing to attend classes, maintain passing grades, and plan for their future to stay eligible for the team. This suggests that competitive games are not a distraction, but instead a new pathway to help students stay engaged in school and build long-term goals for their careers.

questions.title: Children should spend more time outdoors
questions.summary: Children should spend more time exploring outdoors instead of staying indoors for too much academic learning.
questions.text:
Children should spend more time exploring outdoors instead of staying indoors for too much academic learning. In the past, children spent much of their free time playing outside, observing nature, running with friends, and learning from real-life experiences. These outdoor activities helped them develop curiosity, independence, and a stronger connection with the world around them.

However, many children today spend most of their time indoors because of homework, tutoring classes, and pressure to improve academic performance. Instead of climbing trees, playing sports, or exploring parks, they often sit for long hours at desks, using books, computers, or tablets. This change has reduced their chances to move freely and experience the natural environment.

Spending too much time indoors can negatively affect children’s physical and mental development. Lack of outdoor activity may lead to weaker fitness, poor eyesight, stress, and lower creativity. Children also lose important opportunities to build social skills, solve problems independently, and learn how to cooperate with others through play.

Therefore, parents and schools should encourage children to spend more time outdoors. Academic learning is important, but it should not replace outdoor exploration. A healthy childhood needs a balance between study and play, because children learn not only from books, but also from nature, movement, and real-world experiences.
